documentary_plan: Append three top-level source_order sections after the last accepted section. Do not touch existing entries. Any source_order edit changes source_order_sha256 inside every realization payload, so make all the edits in one change and re-review once.

Section A, corresp siddur:rosh_hashanah/nesiat_kappayim, heading 'סדר נשיאת כפים.' (s346, printed_page '20', page_start true). Order: instruction s346_opening_rubric → unit tikkun → instruction laws_ascent → unit yehi_ratzon_shel_haqahal → instruction laws_blessing (source_pages s346→s347, which emits the s347 pb n=21 inside the note) → caller np_avodah (retzeh, speaker הש״ץ.) → provider vetearev (with chatimah) → caller np_hodaah [Modim derabbanan (speaker הקהל., s347), Modim (s347 → s348 break before נִסֶּֽיךָ, which needs E2), veal_kullam, ukhetov (conditional with label 'בר״ה ויו״כ.'), vekhol_hachayyim] → provider elohenu/kohanim call → instruction 'הכהנים מברכין.' → provider kohanim berakhah → pesuqim group yevarekhekha (s348) → instruction dream_rubric → unit dream prayer → pesuqim group yaer (opens s349, so its first fragment emits pb n=23) → navigation ribbono_cue → pesuqim group yissa (with the marked Proverbs 3:4) → unit parnassah (s349 → pb n=24 inside → s350, then the instruction and the amen) → instruction german_rubric → caller addir_bamarom → instruction kohanim_turn → provider departure → instruction shoes_rubric → sim_shalom (a caller or a provider, after the gate) → instruction 'בר״ה וי״כ.' followed by besefer (pending the human decision).

Modim / Modim derabbanan linearization: Modim derabbanan (left column, entirely on s347) comes before the chazan's Modim (right column, s347 continuing to s348). This keeps the page sequence monotone. The proposal's alternative, a caller-owned 'page_break' s348 placed after a whole-Modim transclusion, puts about 35 words of s348 on s347. Reject it.

Section B, corresp siddur:rosh_hashanah/shir_shel_yom, heading 'שיר של יום.' (s351, no n). A flat order: [German label, Hebrew rubric, citation note 'כד', existing unit psalm_24], [Monday label and rubric, psalm_48 (pb s352 inside verse 11)], [Tuesday, psalm_82], [Wednesday, psalm_94 (pb s353 inside verse 23)], [Thursday label and rubric, psalm_81], [Friday label (instruction page_start true, s354, no n), rubric, caller for Psalm 93], [Shabbat label and rubric, caller for Psalm 92]. Do not give day sub-sections a corresp equal to a caller URN, because a duplicate corresp in the project fails validation. Do not use 'page_break' entries on s351–s355, because they pass n=None.

Section C, corresp siddur:rosh_hashanah/kaddish, heading 'קדיש.' (s355, no n): caller kaddish/preface → instruction 'יתו' (description) → provider kaddish/yatom → instruction after_study (English with a Hebrew span) → provider al_yisrael → navigation kaddish_resume.

Mapping-only edits to protected legacy units, all fields in SEGMENT_MAPPING_FIELDS: add corresp=<addir URN> to the he and en segments of musaf_kohanim_addir_bamarom. Optionally add source=<chosen URN> to musaf_kohanim_dreams, musaf_kohanim_ribbon_haolam and segment 1 of musaf_kohanim_yehi_ratzon. These units are review_encoding, so their realization payloads go stale and need re-review. That gate is the intended one.
Leave validate_baseline and the 518-stem baseline file unchanged. After acceptance, snapshot only the new stems.
Hebrew only: no English units for s346–s355, and no substitute translations.
expanded_plan: Kaddish Yatom: a section whose order is [reference prayer:kaddish/yatom] (the whole s355 unit). Include the preface only where the book prints it, before the appendix Kaddish.

Kaddish Derabbanan: a section with no navigation. Order: rubric (instruction after_study, without source_pages) → reference {target prayer:kaddish/yitgaddal, targetEnd prayer:kaddish/yitbarakh}, which resolves to kaddish_chatzi, the only corresp home → reference prayer:kaddish/derabbanan/al_yisrael → reference {target prayer:kaddish/yatom/yehe_shelama, targetEnd prayer:kaddish/yatom/oseh_shalom}, which is the s355 printing. Before acceptance, verify by compiling that a range starting inside kaddish_chatzi's unit-level j:conditional resolves correctly, and that the speaker_before_reference note stays outside it. Settings for the optional spans: caller defaults are injected automatically; the section may declare them explicitly instead.

Shir shel yom: one section per day, with conditions opensiddur:day-of-week {hebrew-day: N}. Content: the Hebrew day rubric, then reference bible:psalms/N@<he project>. Psalms 92 and 93 resolve to the canonical host, and the host default wording is injected. Day 1 of Rosh Hashanah can only fall on days 2, 3, 5 or 7, so the others resolve false, but encode them anyway. Place it where the expanded order already places psalm_24, if it does; otherwise this needs the human decision on placement.

Priestly blessing material, guarded by opensiddur:practice {birkat-kohanim: true}. The preparation formula becomes complete per role through the kohen condition. The dream prayer is repeated in full at ויחנך through a reference entry, not navigation. Use canonical identities only, never the appendix caller units' own copies. Whether to splice this material into the accepted Musaf repetition or keep it as an appendix section is a human question. Where the Musaf repetition already sets a text (dreams, parnassah, addir, departure, third-verse responses), do not set it twice.

English parallel: alignment comes only from existing same-edition English providers that share the prayer: or bible: identity (retzeh, modim, veal_kullam, ukhetov, Psalms 92/93, the kaddish_chatzi parts, and addir after its corresp is added). Everything else stays absent.
Any expanded_order edit invalidates every realization review, because expanded_order_sha256 is in every payload. Land it together with the source_order edit.

required_code_changes.id: RC-C (code, required only for exact Modim pagination under the overlay route), E2: printing page breaks in canonical homes
required_code_changes.change: This implements the SIDDUR_URN_SCHEME 'One text, printed on several pages' mechanism for homes. Add readings.canonical_printings items {id, host stem, lang, identity, fragment index if the host has several, caller stem, scan, printed_page|null, before: an exact host substring that occurs once}. In realizations.validate_occurrences, allow a canonical occurrence with N fragments when exactly N−1 printings are declared for that caller and identity. The joined caller text must equal canonical_text, and each caller fragment boundary must map to its declared 'before' offset in the resolved text, which must not fall inside an overlay's printed span. In home generation, emit <pb ed='1965 <caller page_context>' n? facs> before 'before'. The caller emits no pb for fragments after the first. In validate_generated, replace 'no pb in canonical home' with: allowed only when ed has a second token equal to a declaring caller's context, matched one-to-one with the declared printings. Include the printings in the realization payloads of host and caller.
required_code_changes.risk: Homes stop being pb-free, so exporter scan_links must suppress pbs whose sigil belongs to another printing.
required_code_changes.tests: The documentary appendix compile shows the s348 pb exactly before נִסֶּֽיךָ. The rh_hodaah context still shows only its s32 pb. The expanded output shows no appendix pb. Home XML is unchanged when no printings are declared. A misplaced 'before' or an overlap with an overlay is rejected.

required_code_changes.id: RC-D (code, recommended for the overlay route), E1: several disjoint overlays per host fragment
required_code_changes.change: In realizations.prepare_unit, replace 'len(spans) != 1' with this check: every printed span occurs once, and the spans do not overlap by offset. Sort the alternatives by offset before build's sequential split. canonical_text applies replacements by offset, right to left, instead of chained str.replace. bind_corrections already iterates every overlay.
required_code_changes.tests: Two disjoint overlays produce two choices in text order. Overlapping overlays are rejected. Every selection combination round-trips the literal. Existing single-overlay outputs are byte-identical.

required_code_changes.id: RC-E (small fix, required if overlay 'printings' are used for unnumbered pages)
required_code_changes.change: In build.unit_document, skip the biblScope for source_printings whose printed_page is None. Today it passes from/to=None to lxml.

Printed reference marks: add an optional citation key 'n', emitted as note/@n and included in instruction_review_text, and include a segment's 'anchor' in unit_review_text only when a new 'printed_mark' key is present, so existing review texts stay stable. Without this, the '*)' and '*' glyphs are represented only by anchors, and no review sees them.

Let validate_occurrence_controls accept operator structures {operator, conditions} recursively. This is needed only if 'high-holidays' does not mean RH and YK, so that ukhetov can carry any(holiday.rosh-hashana, holiday.yom-kippur).

Three extensions are not needed under this plan. E9: allow canonical hosts that carry language, speaker_before_reference and unit conditions (kaddish_chatzi); this would weaken the Ten Days guard. E8: allow host fragments with quotations; not needed while the appendix provides the departure prayer. E3: partial-segment canonical occurrences for besefer; a human decision comes first. Do not change validate_baseline, and do not add fields to UNIT_MAPPING_FIELDS.

review_concerns: The proposal says the s350 parentheses are 'mother-only', but working-pages (with human836–845 applied) shows '(וִימֵי אָבִי וְאִמִּי)', the same as s314. Settle this before binding optional controls.

Under the current one-overlay-per-segment rule, the meteg-heavy reprints (Retzeh, Modim, Modim derabbanan) need near-whole-paragraph overlays. These put both full printings inside the canonical home as j:option. That is legal but misleading, so prefer E1, or get an explicit policy decision.

The registry has separate prayer:kaddish/derabbanan/yehe_shelama and oseh_shalom alongside the yatom ones. The Ashkenaz text is the same, which may violate the nesting rule. Do not emit the derabbanan versions here.
Role labels inside provider ranges leak into every transclusion. Use speaker_before_reference at identity boundaries. The ותערב chatimah needs its own identity for this to work.

The day rubric 'היום … שבו הלוים היו אומרים במקדש' is recited aloud in practice, but it was accepted as an instruction. That is fine for the documentary output; the expanded output may need it as recited text.

In the laws, 'ה׳ אוירים' (five), 'בג׳ עשה' and 'כ״ט ב׳' (footnote) are numerals and must not be tagged as Names. 'ישא ה׳ פניו' and 'בסוד ה׳' are Names. In instructions, tag each one explicitly, never by a global rule.

The segment-level source_reference_part still puts the whole verse URN on the verse milestone when no source_reference_corresp is given (a latent bug; quotation_words already guards against it). For partial verses, use explicit context URNs or quotation_words.
The overlay 'printings' (printed_page null) and the order entries 'page_break' (n=None) both fail on the unnumbered pages s351–s355.
The appendix pagination (20–24) repeats page numbers from the main sequence. Only the facs value tells them apart.

Expanded Derabbanan takes the kaddish_chatzi wording for its first three paragraphs (דִּי־בְרָא, not this printing's דִּבְרָא). This is acceptable for an editorial expanded text, but it must be stated in the expanded coverage note.

'(ולכון)' is small and unpointed, while '(וְאַרְעָא)' is normal size and pointed. The different typography may mean a variant reading rather than an optional word; both are encoded as optional for now.
vekhol_hachayyim and besefer have only legacy siddur: identities as hosts. Callers to them are tolerated, but no new siddur holders are created.
human_questions: Policy for typographic reprints of identities already emitted (Retzeh, Modim, Modim derabbanan): approve (A) canonical callers with overlays (recommended: with E1, and E2 for the Modim page break), or (B) a narrowly guarded documentary-printing exception, a literal witness with seg@source and a consonantal-skeleton equality check that is never used in the expanded book. notes: Zero-code paths that already fit the APIs: new biblical units (Psalms 48, 82, 94, 81); canonical callers with one overlay per verse for Psalms 92/93 and Psalm 25:6; an exact pointer for Numbers 14:17; single-span overlays for veal_kullam, ukhetov, vekhol and addir; Modim derabbanan with one overlay per host fragment; first-emission providers for kaddish/yatom, its closings, al_yisrael and yehi_ratzon_shel_haqahal; paginated laws through source_pages; navigation entries for the documentary cues.

General rule applied: when a prayer identity is not yet emitted in this project, the appendix printing provides it (corresp), and earlier legacy siddur-holder printings may gain only source attribution. When the identity is already emitted, or the earlier printing differs in a single span and has same-edition English (addir), the earlier printing hosts and the appendix calls.
Caller units have siddur: URNs and no words of their own, so they pass the scheme's 'remove transclusions' test. Their page breaks get the ed sigil automatically from unit_urn.
Every mapping change proposed for protected units uses fields in UNIT_MAPPING_FIELDS or SEGMENT_MAPPING_FIELDS. Those units are review_encoding, so their realization payloads still force re-review.
limitations: I did not read readings.json, reviews.json, the current source_order, expanded_order, navigation or wording_variants. So I cannot confirm that no existing overlay sits on retzeh, modim or the psalm hosts, where Sim Shalom and ותערב already live, or where the expanded order places psalm_24.
